page: Running Hono on Cloudflare Pages edge platform for full-stack web applications. Note: Cloudflare recommends Cloudflare Workers for new projects. Pages serves static files and dynamic content from Workers. Supports Vite dev server and Wrangler deployment. Setup: npm create hono@latest my-app, select cloudflare-pages template. Directory: public/static for assets, src/index.tsx for server entry, renderer.tsx for layout. Hello World: Hono app with app.get(), c.render() JSX support. Run: npm run dev, access http://localhost:5173. Deploy: npm run deploy or Cloudflare dashboard GitHub integration. Bindings: Variables, KV, D1 via wrangler.toml. Configuration: vite.config.ts with @hono/vite-dev-server, @hono/vite-cloudflare-pages. Client-side scripts: Vite entry points, import.meta.env.PROD detection. Middleware: Cloudflare Pages middleware via handleMiddleware, supports Hono middleware. EventContext access via c.env. Questions: How do I set up Cloudflare Pages? How do I use bindings? How do I deploy? How do I write client-side code? How do I use middleware?

sections.manifest: Project setup for Cloudflare Pages. Create: npm create hono@latest my-app, select cloudflare-pages template. Install dependencies: npm i (or yarn, pnpm, bun). Directory structure: package.json, public/static (assets), src/index.tsx (entry), src/renderer.tsx (layout), tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts. Access static files: /static/file.css mapped to public/static/file.css. Questions: How do I create project? Where do assets go? What's the entry point?

Hello World on Cloudflare Pages. File: src/index.tsx. Import renderer, Hono. Create app: new Hono(). Renderer middleware: app.get('*', renderer). Route: app.get('/', (c) => c.render(

Hello!

)). Export: export default app. JSX rendering via c.render() method. Questions: How do I set up hello world? How do I use renderer? How do I render JSX?

Development and deployment. Dev: npm run dev, access http://localhost:5173 (Vite). Deploy methods: (1) npm run deploy via CLI with package manager specified in package.json. (2) GitHub integration: dashboard Workers & Pages > Pages > Connect to Git, provide build command (npm run build), build directory (dist), production branch (main). Questions: How do I run locally? How do I deploy? What's the build directory?

Cloudflare Bindings (Variables, KV, D1). Create wrangler.toml: wrangler kv namespace create MY_KV --preview for KV, [vars] MY_NAME = "value" for variables. Configure vite.config.ts: devServer with entry and cloudflare adapter, build plugin. Type bindings: type Bindings = { MY_NAME: string, MY_KV: KVNamespace }. Use in app: new Hono<{ Bindings }>(), access via c.env.MY_NAME, c.env.MY_KV.get/put(). Local vs production: wrangler.toml for dev, dashboard for production. Questions: How do I set up KV? How do I use variables? How do I configure vite? How do I access bindings?

Client-side scripts with Vite. Entry point: /src/client.ts. Detect build phase: import.meta.env.PROD (true in build, false in dev). Script tags: conditional src (PROD: '/static/client.js', dev: '/src/client.ts'). Build configuration: vite.config.ts with mode 'client' for client build, rollupOptions.input/output. Build command: vite build --mode client && vite build. Questions: How do I add client scripts? How do I detect build mode? How do I configure build?

Cloudflare Pages middleware system. File: functions/_middleware.ts. Export: onRequest function. handleMiddleware: wraps Hono middleware for Pages. Usage: export const onRequest = handleMiddleware(async (c, next) => {...}). Built-in middleware: basicAuth, others. Multiple middleware: export const onRequest = [handleMiddleware(m1), handleMiddleware(m2), ...]. EventContext access: c.env.eventContext.data. Questions: How do I use middleware? What's handleMiddleware? How do I access EventContext? How do I add multiple middleware?

EventContext in Pages middleware and handlers. Middleware sets data: c.env.eventContext.data.user = 'value'. Handler accesses: c.env.eventContext.data.user. Type: EventContext from 'hono/cloudflare-pages'. Bindings type: { eventContext: EventContext }. Handle function: handle(app) exports onRequest. Questions: How do I pass data between middleware? How do I access EventContext data? How do I type EventContext?
